scenes.text: Two melons. Five point eight million yen.
They're Yubari King melons, grown in heated greenhouses in Hokkaido, Japan.
Each one rests on its own little mat, so it grows perfectly round.
Farmers even control the sunlight. Too much and the netting won't form. Too little and the sugar never develops.
Every melon is checked by hand. Weight, shape, sugar, color. Fail, and it loses the name.
An everyday one costs four to five thousand yen. The first pair of the season sold for five point eight million. Would you pay it for fruit? Yes or no.
